title: ABS vs. PVC: Choosing the Right DWV Piping Material
description: Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS) and Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) are two common thermoplastic materials used in modern drain, waste, and vent (DWV) systems. While both handle household wastewater effectively, key material differences affect installation. ABS is a one-step solvent weld process, lighter in weight, and handles cold temperatures well without shattering. PVC requires a two-step primer and cement process, offers higher rigidity, and has superior sound-dampening qualities. Never mix ABS and PVC without approved transition couplings or special transition solvent cement approved by local plumbing codes.

ABS vs. PVC: Choosing the Right DWV Piping Material

Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS) and Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) are two common thermoplastic materials used in modern drain, waste, and vent (DWV) systems. While both handle household wastewater effectively, key material differences affect installation. ABS is a one-step solvent weld process, lighter in weight, and handles cold temperatures well without shattering. PVC requires a two-step primer and cement process, offers higher rigidity, and has superior sound-dampening qualities. Never mix ABS and PVC without approved transition couplings or special transition solvent cement approved by local plumbing codes.
